expertInsight: Pardot is now officially Marketing Cloud Account Engagement (MCAE) — Salesforce made the rename in 2022. The exam code (CRT-302) and 'Pardot Consultant' title haven't changed, so that's still what you'll search for and what shows up on your credential. Just don't be thrown when every screenshot in Trailhead or the product itself says Account Engagement instead of Pardot.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Account Engagement Consultant Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The Account Engagement Consultant exam is challenging. It tests strategic solution design for B2B marketing automation, including lead scoring and grading models, Engagement Studio program architecture, Salesforce sync configuration, and campaign attribution. Hands-on implementation experience is essential.
bullets: 68% passing score — slightly higher than some consultant exams, reflecting the depth of B2B marketing automation knowledge required.
Solution design focus — expect scenario questions asking you to design scoring models, multi-path Engagement Studio programs, and Salesforce sync architectures for specific business requirements.
CRM alignment tested — you must understand Pardot-Salesforce campaign alignment, the connector user’s permissions, and how B2B Marketing Analytics extends attribution reporting.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Complete at least two full Pardot implementations covering scoring, Engagement Studio, and Salesforce sync before booking. Score 80%+ on practice exams to account for the higher passing threshold.

examFormat.heading: Account Engagement Consultant Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or in-person. Here is the format:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: About 55-65% of questions are scenario-based. You’ll be given a B2B marketing requirement and asked to design a scoring model, recommend an Engagement Studio program structure, or configure the Salesforce sync architecture.
bestWayToPass: Master scoring and grading design: Know how to configure scoring categories, custom scoring rules, and grading profiles that align with a client’s sales qualification criteria.
Design Engagement Studio programs: Practice building multi-branch nurture programs with conditional logic, re-engagement paths, and entry/exit criteria for complex B2B scenarios.

Understand Salesforce sync deeply: Know the connector user’s required permissions, field sync behavior settings (Pardot wins, Salesforce wins, Most Recently Updated), and how to troubleshoot sync errors.
Study campaign attribution: Know the difference between Pardot first-touch campaigns and Salesforce multi-touch campaigns, and how Connected Campaigns and B2B Marketing Analytics extend reporting.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers strategic B2B marketing automation design with Account Engagement (Pardot), including lead scoring models, Engagement Studio nurture programs, Salesforce sync architecture, and campaign attribution.

keyConcepts.h2: Pardot Consultant: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Implementation and Configuration
blocks.body: The [Pardot Consultant](/certifications/pardot-consultant) exam focuses on strategic configuration beyond the Specialist level. Implementation includes Business Unit setup, connector configuration (Pardot-Salesforce sync settings), user management across roles (Admin, Marketing, Sales), and account-level settings. The consultant designs the overall marketing automation architecture — single vs multi-business unit strategy, campaign attribution model, and integration with Salesforce CRM campaigns. Know the difference between Pardot Admin permissions and Salesforce Connected User permissions.

blocks.heading: Advanced Lead Nurturing Strategy
blocks.body: Consultant-level Engagement Studio design covers multi-path programmes, re-engagement campaigns, and cross-business-unit nurturing. Advanced scenarios include pause/resume logic, entry source management (lists, segments, dynamic entry), and Engagement Studio reporting (completions, active, stopped). The consultant selects between Engagement Studio, Automation Rules, and Segmentation Rules for complex nurturing requirements. Know when Salesforce Flow (triggered from Pardot via the connector) is more appropriate than Pardot-native automation.

blocks.heading: Pardot-Salesforce Campaign Alignment
blocks.body: Pardot Campaigns track first-touch attribution. Salesforce Campaigns track multi-touch attribution and enable influence reporting. Pardot Campaign Influence connects Pardot prospect activity to Salesforce Opportunities — configured via Campaign Influence settings. B2B Marketing Analytics (built on [CRM Analytics](/certifications/crm-analytics-einstein-discovery-consultant)) provides advanced attribution dashboards. The consultant designs the campaign data model — Campaign Hierarchy, campaign member statuses, and attribution window settings — to align marketing and sales reporting.

blocks.heading: Advanced Scoring, Grading, and Segmentation
blocks.body: Scoring Categories maintain separate score totals per product or business unit. Custom scoring rules allow point adjustments for specific activities beyond defaults. Profile criteria drive grading — the consultant designs the grade thresholds (A through F) and profile attributes that match the ideal customer profile. Segmentation Rules create static lists from criteria at a point in time (unlike Dynamic Lists which are ongoing). The consultant architects the scoring and grading model to align with sales qualification criteria.

blocks.heading: Reporting, ROI, and B2B Marketing Analytics
blocks.body: The Pipeline Report connects Pardot activities to Salesforce Opportunities — showing which campaigns generated pipeline. Engagement History embedded on Salesforce records shows individual prospect activity timelines. B2B Marketing Analytics (**Einstein Analytics** for B2B) provides pre-built dashboards for engagement, pipeline influence, and campaign performance. The consultant designs the reporting strategy to demonstrate marketing ROI to leadership and aligns metrics to business outcomes (MQL-to-SQL rate, campaign attribution, pipeline influence %).

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Marketing Cloud Account Engagement Consultant Exam
scenarioTips.intro: The Account Engagement (Pardot) Consultant exam tests solution design for B2B marketing automation. Scenarios ask you to design nurture programs, lead scoring models, and Salesforce sync configurations for specific business requirements.

blocks.heading: Lead Scoring & Grading Design
blocks.body: Scoring measures prospect engagement (activity-based); Grading measures fit (demographic-based). Know how to configure scoring categories, custom scoring rules, and grading profiles to align sales and marketing on lead quality.

blocks.heading: Engagement Studio (Nurture Programs)
blocks.body: Know all Engagement Studio trigger, rule, and action types. Understand how to design multi-branch programs, set wait times, and use rules to route prospects based on behavior or CRM data.

blocks.heading: Salesforce Sync Architecture
blocks.body: Understand the sync between Pardot (Prospects) and Salesforce (Leads/Contacts), sync triggers (Salesforce Connector user, **assignment rules**), and how to troubleshoot sync errors. Know the connector user's required permissions.

blocks.heading: Forms, Landing Pages & Tracking
blocks.body: Know how to configure Pardot forms vs. form handlers (for external forms), landing page redirects, custom redirects for tracking links, and how the Pardot tracking pixel works across sites.

blocks.heading: Campaign Reporting & Attribution
blocks.body: Understand Pardot campaign metrics, the Engagement History component, and how B2B Marketing Analytics extends reporting. Know the difference between first-touch and multi-touch attribution models.

sampleQuestions.question: A client's sales team ignores the lead scores entirely. What should the consultant investigate first?
options: Whether the sales team has been given enough training on the Account Engagement interface
Whether the scoring model matches how sales qualifies
Whether the client has purchased sufficient Engagement Studio licences for the team
Whether the scoring rules are being recalculated often enough to stay current
sampleQuestions.explanation: Scores get ignored when they do not predict anything sales recognises, so the model has to reflect what actually signals a real opportunity.
whyWrong: Training does not help if the numbers are not useful.
Licensing does not affect whether scores are credible.
Recalculation frequency is rarely the reason a model is distrusted.

sampleQuestions.question: What should drive the design of a grading profile?
options: The volume of prospects the client expects to generate each month
The order in which the client's sales regions were established
The attributes of the client's best existing customers
The number of fields the client currently captures on its web forms
sampleQuestions.explanation: Grading measures fit, so it is built from the characteristics that distinguish the customers the business actually wants more of.
whyWrong: Volume is a capacity question rather than a fit question.
Regional history has no bearing on customer fit.
Form fields are a means of capture, not a definition of fit.

sampleQuestions.question: A client wants marketing-qualified leads passed to sales automatically. What is the cleanest mechanism?
options: A manual review meeting held each week to agree which leads to hand over
An automation rule assigning on score and grade
A segmentation rule run each morning to build a static list for the team
A completion action on every form the client has published on its website
sampleQuestions.explanation: Automation rules continually evaluate prospects and can assign them once they cross the agreed score and grade threshold.
whyWrong: A weekly meeting delays the handover and does not scale.
A static list does not react as prospects qualify through the day.
Completion actions fire per asset and cannot express a combined threshold.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the risk of syncing every Account Engagement field back to Salesforce?
options: The connector being disabled automatically once a field limit is reached
Noise in the CRM and avoidable sync volume
Account Engagement losing the ability to score any of the prospects involved
Salesforce refusing to accept records that contain marketing-specific fields
sampleQuestions.explanation: Sales users need the few fields that help them act, and syncing everything buries those among data nobody uses.
whyWrong: No automatic disabling occurs.
Scoring continues regardless of what is synced.
Salesforce accepts the fields; the problem is their usefulness.

sampleQuestions.question: A client has one Account Engagement instance and three business units with different brands. What should the consultant check?
options: Whether each brand has been given its own separate Salesforce organisation
Whether the client has enough custom fields remaining for all three brands
Whether business units are configured to separate them
Whether the three brands can share a single tracker domain between them
sampleQuestions.explanation: Business units separate prospects, assets and permissions, which is what distinct brands with distinct audiences require.
whyWrong: Separate orgs would fragment the client's CRM unnecessarily.
Field capacity is not the structural concern here.
Tracker domains matter but are not the separation mechanism.

sampleQuestions.question: Why would a consultant recommend progressive profiling on a client's forms?
options: Short forms convert better while still building the record
It allows the client to capture data without recording any consent at all
It removes the need to score or grade any of the prospects who submit
It guarantees that every prospect record will be complete after one visit
sampleQuestions.explanation: Asking for a few new fields each visit keeps conversion high while the profile fills out over time.
whyWrong: Consent requirements apply however the data is gathered.
Scoring and grading are unaffected by how fields are collected.
The whole point is that the profile completes gradually.

sampleQuestions.question: A client reports that prospects are being assigned to sales users who have left. What should be reviewed?
options: The scoring thresholds that determine when a prospect is assigned at all
The tracker domain configuration used across the client's landing pages
The assignment rules and the user records behind them
The frequency with which the Salesforce connector performs its sync
sampleQuestions.explanation: Assignment points at specific users or queues, so departures have to be reflected there or prospects go nowhere useful.
whyWrong: Thresholds decide when to assign, not to whom.
Tracker domains concern tracking rather than ownership.
Sync frequency does not determine assignment targets.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a consultant need to establish before designing an Engagement Studio programme?
options: The number of emails the client would like to send each month
The total number of prospects currently held in the database
The colour scheme the client uses across its marketing templates
The decision the prospect is being helped to make
sampleQuestions.explanation: A nurture programme exists to move someone towards a decision, so the content and branching follow from what that decision is.
whyWrong: Send volume is an output of the design rather than an input.
Database size does not determine the programme's purpose.
Visual design is a separate concern from programme logic.

sampleQuestions.question: A client's unsubscribe rate rises sharply after a new nurture programme launches. What is the likely cause?
options: Frequency or relevance has moved in the wrong direction
The tracker domain has not been verified for the client's sending domain
The programme was built without using any wait steps between the emails
The prospects involved were graded before the programme was activated
sampleQuestions.explanation: People opt out when they get too much mail or mail that does not match their interest, and a new programme changes both.
whyWrong: A tracker domain issue would affect link tracking, not opt-out volume.
Missing waits could contribute, but frequency and relevance is the broader cause.
Grading has no bearing on unsubscribe behaviour.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of a suppression list on a client's email send?
options: To hold the prospects who have not yet been assigned to a sales user
To group the prospects who have the highest scores in the database
To exclude prospects who should not receive it
To record which prospects have already opened a previous send
sampleQuestions.explanation: Suppression lists keep specific prospects out of a send, whether for consent, recency or relevance reasons.
whyWrong: Unassigned prospects are not inherently excluded from sends.
High scorers would be a segment rather than a suppression.
Engagement history is tracked separately.

sampleQuestions.question: A client asks whether to use a form or a form handler on their new campaign landing page. What should decide it?
options: Who controls the page and whether its markup must stay
Whether the campaign is being run for new or for existing prospects
Which of the two options the client's developers prefer to work with
The number of fields the client intends to capture on the page itself
sampleQuestions.explanation: If the page is yours to change, the native form gives you progressive profiling and validation. If the markup must stay, a handler is the way in.
whyWrong: Prospect status does not determine the capture mechanism.
Developer preference is secondary to the actual constraint.
Field count works either way.

sampleQuestions.question: Why does a consultant care about the tracker domain being set up with the client's own domain?
options: It determines how many landing pages the client is permitted to publish
It is the only way for the client to record any prospect activity at all
It allows the client to bypass the consent requirements in their market
Cookies and links then come from a domain prospects trust
sampleQuestions.explanation: A first-party tracker domain means tracking and links appear under the client's own name, which helps both trust and cookie handling.
whyWrong: Page limits are a licensing matter.
Activity can be tracked on the default domain too, just less well.
Consent requirements apply regardless of the domain.

sampleQuestions.question: A client has 200,000 prospects, most of whom have never engaged. What should the consultant propose?
options: A single large send to the whole database to see who responds to it
An increase in the client's send frequency to improve overall engagement
An immediate deletion of every prospect who has not engaged recently
A re-engagement programme, then suppression of the rest
sampleQuestions.explanation: Give dormant prospects a defined chance to re-engage, then stop mailing those who do not, which protects deliverability.
whyWrong: A blanket send to a cold database invites complaints and bounces.
Sending more to disengaged people makes deliverability worse.
Deleting without attempting re-engagement discards recoverable value.

sampleQuestions.question: What should a consultant measure to show the value of marketing automation to a client's board?
options: The number of emails and landing pages the team produced in the period
Pipeline and revenue influenced by marketing activity
The size of the prospect database compared with the previous year
The count of automation rules and programmes currently running
sampleQuestions.explanation: A board cares about pipeline and revenue, so the measures that matter connect marketing activity to opportunities created and won.
whyWrong: Asset production is output rather than outcome.
A larger database is not inherently valuable.
Rule counts describe configuration, not results.

sampleQuestions.question: Which best describes the consultant's role on an Account Engagement implementation?
options: Translating how the client sells into how the tool works
Writing the email and landing page content the client will publish
Managing the client's sending reputation on their behalf after go-live
Configuring every automation rule the client's marketing team requests
sampleQuestions.explanation: The work is understanding the client's buying and selling process and expressing it in scoring, grading, automation and nurture.
whyWrong: Content creation usually remains with the client's marketing team.
Reputation management is an ongoing operational responsibility.
Building whatever is asked for without challenge is order-taking.
